analysis.partName: PRCR002 – complex machined/cast housing (mis-classified as sheet metal by Stage-1)

detectedFeatures.description: Wall thickness varies by two orders of magnitude — incompatible with constant-gauge sheet metal forming
132 cylinders + 55 cones + 34 tori — turned/cast/machined bosses, fillets and shafts, not stamped features
76 organic surfaces — not producible by bend/pierce tooling
44 undercut faces — require side-action tooling or multi-axis machining, impossible in a simple progressive die
10 boss/shaft features up to r=57mm — thick solid sections

primarySuggestion.name: DC01 mild steel (sheet-metal framework material choice)
primarySuggestion.reasoning: No aluminium signal present (no lightweighting note, no thin uniform 2-4mm HPDC wall). Geometry shows thick, dense boss/shaft/threaded features typical of a mechanical/structural component, so per guidance we default to steel rather than aluminium. However, the wall-thickness spread (0.45–170mm) and face mix (cylinders/cones/tori/B-splines, 44 undercuts) is fundamentally inconsistent with sheet metal — this is almost certainly a cast-and-machined or forged steel part, not a stamping. DC01 is used here only to satisfy the forced sheet-metal cost framework.

alternatives.name: SG iron (ductile cast iron) - if cast

processRecommendations.process: Sheet metal progressive stamping (as instructed by Stage-1)
processRecommendations.reasoning: Stage-1 classifier flagged sheet_metal, but geometry (non-uniform 0.45–170mm walls, 132 cylinders, 55 cones, 34 tori, 76 free-form faces, 44 undercuts, threaded bosses) is not achievable by blank/bend/pierce tooling. Retained only because required by task framework.

High free-form content, undercuts, cored bosses and variable wall sections strongly indicate a cast (steel/ductile iron) part finished by CNC drilling/threading — a far better geometric fit than stamping.
Bottom-up CNC estimate (1.068hr, 3 setups) already computed and is a viable fallback if low-volume prototyping is required before tooling investment.

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Part geometry (wall thickness σ=46.6mm, cylinders/cones/tori, 44 undercuts) is incompatible with sheet-metal stamping despite Stage-1 classification
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Re-classify as casting or machining before committing to progressive-die tooling

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Cannot be formed by straight punch/die motion; would require multiple secondary hits or complete re-tooling as cast part
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Move to casting with side cores, or split into multiple sheet-metal sub-assemblies

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Extremely thin local section is at risk of tearing during piercing/forming
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Increase local wall to ≥1.0mm or move feature to a separate thinner insert

manufacturabilityRisks.description: Threads cannot be formed in-die; require secondary tapping/thread-forming operation not covered by the stamping cycle
manufacturabilityRisks.suggestion: Add post-forming tapping station or use self-clinching/flow-form inserts

dfmIssues.description: Undercut faces cannot be released from a straight-motion progressive die; would require side-action tooling or a full process change to casting/machining.
dfmIssues.recommendation: Re-route part to casting or multi-axis machining process before tooling commitment

dfmIssues.description: Two-order-of-magnitude wall variation is incompatible with constant-gauge sheet forming and will cause tearing, buckling or non-fill in a stamped blank.
dfmIssues.recommendation: Abandon sheet-metal process; use casting with cored sections or machine from solid

dfmIssues.description: Organic surfaces cannot be produced by bend/pierce tooling and imply a cast or machined origin.
dfmIssues.recommendation: Model part as cast/machined component and re-run cost estimate under cast_and_machine commodity

dfmIssues.description: High count of turned/cast features (bosses, fillets, shafts) indicates a rotationally-machined or cast part, not a stamping.
dfmIssues.recommendation: Use casting + CNC finishing process chain

dfmIssues.description: Threads and bored holes require secondary machining operations not part of the stamping cycle.
dfmIssues.recommendation: Add tapping/boring operations to process plan regardless of primary forming method

dfmIssues.description: 25 bends per part — Many bends multiply press-brake handling, tool changes and cumulative angle tolerance.
dfmIssues.fix: Reduce bend count, group same-tool bends, or move to a stamping die if volume supports it.

deterministicAnalysis.aiExplanation:
Derived deterministically for sheet_metal from the measured geometry. No AI call was made; every figure below is arithmetic on a measurement or a library lookup, and each states its own basis.

  • sheetMetal.blankLengthMm = 291 — largest bounding-box dimension × 1.05 trim allowance [geometry, sm-blank-l]
  • sheetMetal.blankWidthMm = 234 — second-largest bounding-box dimension × 1.05 trim allowance [geometry, sm-blank-w]
  • sheetMetal.numOps = 12 — 1 blank + 25 bend(s) + 1 pierce = 12 stations [geometry, sm-num-ops]
  • sheetMetal.strokesPerMin = 29 — feed-limited: 18 m/min ÷ 321 mm pitch, de-rated for 25 bends [rule, sm-spm]

Still open (1):
  • What is this part made of? — A CAD file carries shape, not substance. We measured 1037 cm³ exactly, but the same solid weighs 2.80 kg in aluminium and 8.14 kg in steel. Nothing in the geometry distinguishes them, and guessing wrong moves the material cost several-fold.
analysisLimitations: Unanswered: What is this part made of?

DFM checks ran against the measured geometry. Checks that need a drawing callout — tolerances, which face is critical, whether a weld line is in a load path — did not run, so this list is a floor and not a ceiling.
